About Colin McEvedy

Colin McEvedy (1930-2005) was a psychiatrist, historian and demographer. His many books included the Penguin atlases of Ancient History , Medieval History and Modern History , African History , North American History , the Pacific, The Atlas of World Population History (written with Richard Jones) and The Atlas of World History (written with Sarah McEvedy).

Early life

Colin Peter McEvedy was born in Salford , Lancashire on 6 June 1930. He was the third son of Peter George McEvedy, a renowned surgeon, who was born in New Zealand. [1] Colin was educated at Harrow School, where he was a scholar, and Magdalen College, Oxford.

|# The Penguin Atlas of Ancient History
Front Cover
Colin McEvedy
Penguin Books , 1967 - History - 96 pages
The Penguin atlas of ancient history illustrates, in a chronological series of maps, the evolution of flux of races in Europe, the Mediterranean area, and the Near East. From 50,000 B.C. to the fourth century A.D. the maps and their accompanying commentaries follow the ages of stone, bronze, and iron, and trace the movements and cultural developments of Mesopotamians, Egyptians, Indians, Hittites, Assyrians, Greeks, Persians, Celts, Etruscans, Carthaginians, Goths, Romans, and many other peoples.
